article.headline: Towering Gilas routs Syria by 39 points in World Cup qualifying debut
article.summary: Gilas Pilipinas cruised to a 97-58 victory over Syria on Friday to improve to a 5-4 record in the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers.
article.body: Kai Sotto needed only 17 minutes and 40 seconds to post a dominant 18-point, 10-rebound performance as the Philippines secured a lopsided victory at Karisma Arena in Seremban, Malaysia. The win marked the third consecutive victory for the squad, moving them above .500 in the Group E standings with a 5-4 record, while Syria remained at the bottom of the group with a 2-7 standing. The matchup featured a commanding display of physical dominance from the Filipino frontcourt, which controlled the boards to out-rebound their opponents significantly. Following a 43-32 halftime lead, Gilas broke the game open with a 29-13 third quarter behind a relentless shooting display from downtown, ultimately leading by as many as 40 points during the contest. This triumph is vital for the Philippines as the team navigates the fifth of six windows in the qualification process. Coach Tim Cone praised the team’s ability to execute within their established systems, specifically highlighting the seamless debut of naturalized player Bennie Boatwright. Boatwright finished his first outing in a national team jersey with a double-double of 16 points and 13 rebounds. The frontcourt depth was further bolstered by the defensive efforts of Mike Phillips and Quentin Millora-Brown, who combined for 13 rebounds and two blocks. Kevin Quiambao also contributed a game-high-tying 18 points, converting 6-of-8 from beyond the arc to help solidify the lopsided result.

news.title: Ball by Ball Commentary & Live Score - NZ vs IND, 2nd Test
India 116-6 at stumps on day two after New Zealand make 356
Indian spin bowling coach admits "error of judgement" in shot selection after poor day 2 at Christchurch
news.og_title: Indian spin bowling coach admits
news.og_desc: After a poor day with the bat for Team India, Indian spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said that while the game is never out of reach till the final ball is bowled, the team had some "errors of judgement" with their shot selection. After the highs of scoring 720/9 at Wellington, India's highest total away from home, Team India produced a poor outing with the bat in the first innings at Christchurch, ending at 116/6 in reply to NZ's first innings score of 356 on day two. Dismissals of KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant in particular hurt India, as they got out while going for a boundary. Skipper Shubman Gill (17), Devdutt Padikkal, Pant (23) and KL Rahul (25) failed to make the most of their starts. Speaking on the day's play during the post-day presser, Sairaj said that it was a "disappointing day" as the team failed to build partnerships and play upto its potential. "You can never say that the game is gone out of reach till the last ball is bowled. But yes, definitely a disappointing day. We could not build up partnerships. I think all the batters got starts; it is just that we could not convert them into big scores. And I think partnerships on wickets like these are very crucial, and that is what I think was a little bit where we could have just done better," he added. "The shot selection, I think every batter has his own plan, and definitely looking at the pitch, they had their plans intact. But yeah, some errors happened, you know, with the judgment. But overall, again, it all boils down to partnerships in these situations. Yes, certain players take an aggressive route. It did not happen, but I think we did not play to our potential," he added. Sairaj admitted that during the first morning, the team failed to bowl tighter lines, and the pitch had seam movement in it to create doubts in batters' minds; as the game progressed, the bowling got better, with bowling being done in the right areas. Still, he feels that Kiwis could have been restricted 30-40 runs shorter. "To be honest, the first morning we could have bowled tighter lines, which didn't happen because the pitch had a lot of seam movement in terms of creating that doubt in the batter's mind. It's just that the lines were slightly wider, but as the game progressed, we did bowl really well into the right areas, created those opportunities, and personally, I thought we did really well to get those five wickets today, this morning, in those 110 runs," he said. "Definitely, we could have been about 30-40 runs short, but I think, you know, we did not take our catches. Whatever chances came our way, we did not capitalise on that, and that hurt us. So this is where we are at the moment. We know the score; we just had a bad day batting-wise, but again, you know, three days more to go, anything is possible," he added. On Rishabh's dismissal, which saw him go aerial for a six when the team was seeming to recover with a partnership between him and KL Rahul, Sairaj said that the batter is a "unique player" and there is a pattern to how he takes his chances, which could not work sometimes. "The demand was there to have a partnership going, and which was going, but I think he is a unique player. You know, after his hundred in the previous game, he is in form. So there is sometimes a pattern to his play where he takes his chances. Sometimes it works for him, sometimes it does not. But yeah, definitely that particular time a partnership was needed. It did not happen today, but I think he is somebody who takes the game away from the opposition when he plays positively and when he sort of really expresses himself. It did not come out for him today, so it is just one of those days," he signed off. Coming to the match, India opted to field first, skittling out Kiwis for 356 runs in their first innings. Skipper Tom Latham (59 in 128 balls, with six fours) and Devon Conway (31 in 79 balls, with four boundaries) put Kiwis to a fine start with a 77-run opening wicket partnership. India had Kiwis down to 184/5, but a 63-run stand between Glenn Phillips (36 in 67 balls, with five fours) and Tom Blundell took them past the 240-run mark. Blundell, playing his 50th Test, played a gritty, marathon knock of 211-ball 89, with 10 fours, stitching useful partnerships with the lower-order batters before NZ was bundled out. Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj also took two wickets, and Washington Sundar got one. At the end of the second session, India was 59/3, with India losing Yashasvi Jaiswal (0), Devdutt Padikkal (21) and skipper Shubman Gill (17), with Matt Henry getting one and Kyle Jamieson picking two wickets. Jamieson and Jacob Duffy blew Team India away, helping New Zealand finish the day two of the second Test at Christchurch with the cream of Indian batting back to the pavillion. At the end of the day, in reply to NZ's 356 in the first innings total, India was 116/6, with Dhruv Jurel (7*) unbeaten. (ANI)

news.title: Virat Kohli recalls watching India's landmark Brisbane Test win in 2021 from hospital during birth of his child
news.og_title: Virat Kohli recalls watching India's landmark Brisbane Test win in 2021 from hospital during birth of his child
news.og_desc: Indian batting icon Virat Kohli recalled watching Men in Blue's landmark win over Australia at Brisbane back in 2021 from a the hospital during the birth of his child, saying that no other Test win has been more special than that one. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India will start in January next year. After losing the previous BGT series in Aussie conditions last year, Team India would be vying to take back the trophy. With the Test team growing in experience, they could take a lot of inspiration from an Indian side from the final Gabba Test five years back, which was practically a second-string side with several key players out due to injuries. Virat also missed that series after the first Test due to birth of his first child. The first Test at Adelaide saw Team India skittle out for an all-time low score of 36 runs and lose by a huge margin, and India's comeback run from the next Test at Melbourne till the Gabba Test is remembered as one of the greatest turnarounds in cricket history. The next three Tests after the Adelaide debacle saw youngsters like Rishabh Pant, a debuting Shubman Gill, Shardul Thakur, Washington Sundar, T Natarajan and Mohammed Siraj deliver inspiring performances despite the psychological odds, injuries and other adversities. In the final Test, India chased down 328 runs courtesy an 89* from Pant and 91 from Gill, ending Australia's unbeaten run at the venue since 32 years and winning the series back-to-back in Australia. In the first innings, a 123-run stand between half-centurions Shardul and Sundar lifted India from 186/6 to 336 in reply to Australia's first innings total of 369. A fifer from Siraj and a four-fer from Shardul bundled out Australia for 294 runs in their second innings, giving India 328 to chase. Speaking to JioStar, Virat, who retired from Test cricket last year with 9,230 runs in 123 Tests and 30 centuries, said, " I was in the hospital for the birth of my child, and I was watching the match on my phone. I watched the partnership between Shardul and Washington until about 15 minutes before we had to go in for the break. That is how special that partnership was. The kind of character and belief shown by the whole squad throughout that series and in that Gabba Test, with so many young players stepping up when nobody gave us a chance, made it one of the most special victories. I do not think any victory has been more special than this." Former Indian head coach Ravi Shastri rated that landmark win as something cricket had never seen before. "At teatime, we knew very clearly that Rishabh Pant was going for the run chase. Washington and Rishabh batted the way they did and backed each other in that last hour of the match. It was unbelievable stuff. There was no fear in their approach, and they were not overawed by the occasion or the Australian attack. You talk about Indian performances. I will go one step further. I don't think cricket has seen anything like this," he added. (ANI)
